summary: Chirapat Prapandvidya works in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He founded Silpakorn University, served there as Director in 1996, and taught Kazuhiro Yamamoto.

Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyodo Koshuin, as well as under Soyen Shaku, Dozan Sugimoto, Nantenbo Nakahara, and Ryushu Hara. He held leadership roles at Soji-ji and founded Tsurumi Women's University.
Chishō Namai specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts at Koyasan University, where he is attested as professor in 1996 and president in 2008.

Chitai Takenaka is an Indologist and philosopher who completed graduate studies at Kyoto University in 1968. He held academic appointments at Hanazono University (attested 1979–1983) and Tokoha University, where he is attested as professor in 1989.

Chizen Akanuma (1884–1937) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Otani University, Kōkōdō, and under Manshi Kiyozawa and Mahagoda Siri Nanissara. A former professor at Otani University, he also co-founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921.

Chizuko Yoshimizu is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology scholar. She studied at Gakushuin University, the University of Tokyo under Zuiho Yamaguchi, and earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna. Her career includes posts at Naritasan Institute, University of Tsukuba, and Toyo Bunko.
Chlodwig H. Werba is an Indologist and linguist who held appointments as professor at the University of Vienna, attested from 1997 through 2022. Among his students was Vitus Angermeier.
Chogye Shabdrung is an active scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 and was taught by Sonam Gyatso.

Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, serving as the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Phenpo Nalendra Monastery from 1928. He studied under teachers including the 13th Dalai Lama, Geshe Tshechok, Zimwok Rinpoche, and Kunga Chöphel.

Chogyu Takayama (1871–1902) was a scholar in philosophy, Japanology, and other fields. He completed his studies at Fukushima Prefectural Asaka High School and the University of Tokyo between 1886 and 1896.
Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and under traditional teacher Daehaeng Kun Sunim (attested 2012).
Choying Wangmo Dorji (1897–1994) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She founded the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as a member of its General Council from 1964 to 1965.
Chris Clark specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon in 2015 and is attested as an honorary associate there in 2019.

Chris Williams is active in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Attested in 2026, he is a postgraduate researcher and teaching staff member at the University of Bristol studying under doctoral supervisor Rita Langer.

Christian August Brandis (1790–1867) was a philosopher who studied at Kiel University. He held academic appointments at the University of Copenhagen, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Bonn.

Christian Bartholomae (1855–1925) was a linguist, Iranian/Central Asian specialist, and Indologist who studied under Heinrich Hübschmann. He held posts at the universities of Halle-Wittenberg, Münster, Giessen, and Heidelberg.

Christian Bernert specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl.

Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen (1791–1860) was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Marburg, Göttingen, Munich, Leiden, and Copenhagen, as well as under Heyne and Silvestre de Sacy, and founded the German Archaeological Institute.

Christian Coseru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Bucharest and the Australian National University under Jay L. Garfield and John Powers, and held positions at the College of Charleston and UC Berkeley.

Christian Friedrich August Dillmann (1823–1894) was a linguist and religious studies scholar who studied under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen, Kiel University, the University of Giessen, and Frederick William University Berlin.
